concept.title: Types of Ransomware
concept.shortdesc: Types of ransomware and the process actors use to block you from accessing files.

conbody.p: A ransomware attack occurs in stages over time and gives actors access to your data. Actors leverage leaking your data against you in exchange for a ransom. Many ransomware attacks begin with phishing users and gaining access to the target system or device using harmful software, known as malware. Once ransomware actors access your device system, they target valuable data such as login credentials, payment methods, and intellectual property. Once actors possess your data, they use your credentials and their software to prevent you from reversing any damage until you pay a ransom, typically through cryptocurrency. Ransomware actors may utilize two general types of attacks: encrypted ransomware requiring users to pay the ransom and receive a key or code to access their data, or non-encrypted ransomware blocking users from accessing anything on the device until paying the ransom. Other forms of ransomware including leakware and wipers produce specialized attacks where actors threaten to dox locations or destroy data. All forms of ransomware risk serious consequences for affected users and range in severity depending on who the attacker(s) and the victim(s) are. Universities include vast collections of personal data allowing ransomware actors to threaten thousands of individuals at once unless the university pays an extreme ransom. You must take precautions to avoid ransomware attacks at the earliest possible stage.
